title: Faster gates: tests forked from preloaded libraries, memory pressure as the limit, the gates' parts side by side, a per-package gate and a gate on a commit in its own worktree
request: The owner found check-all too slow and asked to make the process as fast as possible, using up to 90% of the Mac (8 GB, 8 cores), swap up to 6 GB, yellow memory pressure accepted, only red not.
spec: Cut the time from a finished package to its pushed commit without weakening what the gate proves: every test still runs where it can be affected, PostgreSQL wherever storage behaviour matters, the flows when product code changed, and the whole of check-all at a milestone's end.
plan: Measure where the time goes: 125 files, 8 cores, 8 GB; 111 files waited for memory; two passes of the whole suite in sequence.
Fork every test file from one process that has imported the heavy libraries once.
Start files by macOS's own memory pressure (green and yellow), not by free memory; two workers more than the cores.
Run rd-gates, the agent tests and the flows beside the suite; a per-package gate (affected files, PostgreSQL on the files that check it); a gate on a commit in its own worktree.
Keep what measured faster, revert what measured slower.

decisions.decision: Fork the files from a preloaded forkserver, the project's own modules imported in each child.
decisions.why: Each fresh interpreter loaded pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM and XGBoost again (about 1 GB and seconds each); forked children shared those pages (140 to 200 MB each). The project's modules read the environment at import, so they are not preloaded.

decisions.decision: Memory pressure decides when a file starts: green or yellow, never red.
decisions.why: The owner's rule; free memory undercounts what macOS can compress and swap without slowing down.

decisions.decision: Do not split files below 150 s.
decisions.why: Splitting 87 files repeated their setup: 274 s against 248 s unsplit; the suite is bound by its CPU time (about 2,400 s on 8 cores).

decisions.decision: The import graph chooses the files, but central modules reach most of them.
decisions.why: The session recorder and the contracts' base are imported almost everywhere: most changes reach 110 of 125 files; the saving is in the PostgreSQL pass (30 files that check it) and the flows.

decisions.decision: check-all closes a milestone; check-quick gates a package; check-commit runs a gate on a commit in its own worktree.
decisions.why: Work goes on while the gate runs; a push waits for it.

change: tests/run_parallel.py (forkserver with preloaded libraries, the pressure guard, splitting the slowest files, a unit the system kills runs once more), scripts/affected_tests.py (new: changed files to test files through the imports; --pg, --e2e), Makefile (check-quick, check-quick-tests, check-commit; check-all runs its independent parts beside the suite), CLAUDE.md and the dclab-package skill.

findings.defect: Pushing to 90% of memory by free-memory arithmetic was slower.
findings.scenario: Starting files until 10% was free: 377 s against 328 s.
findings.cause: macOS compresses memory before it swaps, and the guard counted free memory only.
findings.fix: Use the pressure level instead (green and yellow start, red waits).

findings.defect: A file whose tests all passed was reported failed.
findings.scenario: test_staging_check printed OK; the process ended with a signal under load.
findings.cause: The system can end a process under memory pressure; its exit code was read as a failure.
findings.fix: A unit ended by a signal runs once more, and the output says so.

findings.defect: Every recent package would have run everything.
findings.scenario: The import graph reached the whole suite from any change to the server or the contracts.
findings.cause: Those were listed as foundations; the graph already follows their imports.
findings.fix: Foundations only for what no import shows (storage, settings, the runner, requirements).

findings.defect: My Makefile edit broke an f-string with nested quotes.
findings.cause: A sed substitution inside an f-string.
findings.fix: Edit the line in Python, not with sed.

measurements.name: whole suite on files
measurements.gate: faster than 479 s with every test passing
measurements.result: 479 s fresh interpreters; 328 s forked; 248 s forked with the pressure guard and 10 workers
limits: One machine; runs vary from one to the next.

measurements.name: check-all
measurements.result: 645 s with the parts side by side (before the pressure guard)
limits: Measured before the pressure guard and the extra workers.

outcome: A package's gate takes about five minutes and runs in its own worktree while work goes on; the whole suite runs in about half its old time.
lessons: Measure before tuning: the limit moved from memory to the CPU after forking, and more memory made it slower.
A process the system kills is not a failing test: say so and run it again.
risks: Forking after preloading assumes the libraries start no threads at import (one-thread settings are set first).
Two gates at once would share the per-worker test databases: one gate at a time.
